stories.title: Mac Cosmetics’ SoHo Flagship Relocates to 5K SF at 579 Broadway
stories.excerpt: Mac Cosmetics has selected a new foundation in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood. The global makeup brand signed a 5,325-square-foot lease at 579 Broadway between Prince and East Houston streets to host its next flagship location in the trendy shopping corridor, according to an announcement from landlord broker Newmark. The deal represents a relocation of just two blocks from Mac’s current perch alongside Bloomingdale’s at 506 Broadway. The landlord at 579 Broadway, Lord Shivas Properties, was represented by Newmark’s Ariel Schuster, Michael Paster and Logan Ryan. Paster said in a statement that the location, neighbored by brands like jewelry brand Pandora and bohemian clothing store Free People Movement, was a “natural fit for Mac Cosmetics.” The brand plans to occupy approximately 3,825 square feet on the ground floor and 1,500 square feet of lower-level space within the five-story building. The length of Mac’s lease and the asking rent were unclear, but a report from CBRE found retail rents near SoHo’s Prince Street averaged $1,408 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026. Mac will take possession of the storefront in January, according to Newmark. Its current occupant, British fashion retailer AllSaints, will occupy the space through the end of the year. A spokesperson for AllSaints did not immediately respond to a request for comment on its future plans in the neighborhood. Cushman & Wakefield’s Mike O’Neill, Jason Greenstone and Taylor Reynolds negotiated the lease on behalf of Mac Cosmetics. The lease offered Mac the opportunity to secure a highly visible location in the corridor, O’Neill told CO in a statement. “We’re pleased to have helped facilitate a transaction that aligns Mac with a location well positioned to support its long-term retail objectives,” O’Neill said. Lord Shivas Properties also owns the lot’s adjacent storefront at 152 Mercer Street, the site of luxury knitwear brand Extreme Cashmere‘s U.S. flagship. Emily

stories.title: Law Firm DLA Piper, Insurance Group Ascot Ink Deals at 1251 Avenue of the Americas
stories.excerpt: Two office tenants at Mitsui Fudosan America’s 1251 Avenue of the Americas are extending or expanding their footprints, Commercial Observer has learned. Law firm DLA Piper expanded by 41,600 square feet on the entire 29th floor of the Midtown building with an 8.5-year term, bringing the law firm to a total of 210,000 square feet at the property between West 49th and West 50th streets. Meanwhile, insurance company Ascot Group signed a 12-year extension for its 44,100-square-foot offices on the entire 43rd floor, according to sources familiar with the deal. Ascot was previously subleasing the space. Asking rent for Ascot’s space was $150 per square foot, while the asking rent for DLA Piper’s deal was $140 per square foot, according to the source. Newmark‘s David Falk, Pete Shimkin, Eric Cagner and Claire Koeppel are exclusive leasing agents for the 54-story office tower, but declined to comment. CBRE‘s John Nugent and Alexander Golod negotiated on behalf of Ascot, while a separate CBRE team of Mike Wellen and Ken Rapp handled the deal for DLA Piper. CBRE did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the DLA Piper deal and declined to comment on Ascot. Other recent deals at 1251 Avenue of the Americas include a 41,600-square-foot lease for alternative investing firm LGT Capital Partners in May and an expansion to 80,200 square feet for Trust Company of the West in November 2025. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.

stories.title: Value Defines Success for Dining Industry in 2026
stories.excerpt: Value has become a defining theme across the dining industry, the definition of value can vary across the sector’s diverse restaurant categories and for individual brands, Placer.ai says in a new white paper. A closer look at chains across the industry suggests that, amid ongoing economic pressure, perceptions of value are evolving. Titled Dining In 2026: All Roads Lead To Value, the white paper says that consumers in 2026 appear to be evaluating value through a broader lens that includes experience, quality, convenience and affordability. While overall dining traffic this year has trailed 2025 in most months, some segments are doing better than others, such as fast casual and fine dining. Fast casual in particular has seen a number of dining chains maintaining positive traffic momentum by pairing everyday value with the benefits of full-service dining, reports Placer.ai. stories.title: TCC Puts Wrap on Phoenix Sprouts Market, HQ
stories.excerpt: Trammell Crow Company completed a new development anchored by Sprouts Farmers Market in Phoenix. The 8-acre mixed-use development includes a 145,000-square-foot Class A office building serving as Sprouts Farmers Market’s new corporate headquarters, a 25,000-square-foot flagship grocery store, and approximately 11,000 square feet of retail space. The grocery store opened to the public last month, and the headquarters office building is now complete and ready for occupancy. Located within the CityNorth development near 56th Street and Loop 101, the headquarters was designed to support collaboration, innovation, and team member wellness. The office provides a variety of modern workplace amenities tailored to the needs of Sprouts’ growing workforce, including a community garden, rooftop deck, fitness center, and culinary kitchens. Project partners on the Sprouts Farmers Market headquarters development include U.S. Realty Advisors, RSP Architects, Wespac Construction, Inc., Keyser, and JLL. stories.title: Cross Ocean, Fuller Pick Up Massive Houston Office Campus
stories.excerpt: Cross Ocean Partners and Fuller Realty have acquired Eldridge Place, a three-building, 828,784-square-foot office campus in Houston’s Energy Corridor. Commercial Search reports the last time the asset traded hands, in 2019, Granite Properties paid $78.4 million to the seller, TIER REIT. Eldridge Place consists of the 245,315-square-foot One Eldridge Place, the 275,283-square-foot Two Eldridge Place, and the 308,186-square-foot Three Eldridge Place. One and Two were developed in 1986, while Three came online in 2008. Located at 737, 757 and 777 N. Eldridge Parkway, the buildings were 94 percent leased all together at the time of sale. The property’s anchor tenant is Fluor Corp., which occupies about 413,000 square feet, including the entirety of Three Eldridge Place. The buildings have seen more than $20 million of capital improvements since 2019, including renovated lobbies and common areas, elevator modernization and upgraded building systems. Enhanced common-area amenities include a resort-style fitness center, pickleball courts, a full-service deli and a conference facility. stories.title: Former Burned Out Charlotte Apartments Trade for Nearly $500K/Unit
stories.excerpt: Mid-America Apartment Communities acquired Modera Liberty Row from Mill Creek Residential for $116.3 million. That works out to nearly $500,000 a unit. Mill Creek developed Modera Liberty Row in partnership with Hawthorne Residential Partners. It has 239 units across two buildings at 7740 and 7741 Liberty Row Drive. The development has been renamed MAA Liberty Row. Amenities include a pool, fitness center with yoga studio, multiple clubrooms, elevated courtyards, golf simulator lounge, bocce ball courts, coworking spaces, private offices, pet spa and bike storage. The Charlotte Business Observer reports the project was expected to be delivered in spring 2024 before a massive fire destroyed the nearly completed development in May 2023. The building that caught fire was demolished to the concrete slab, and workers removed the wood frame from the second building because of severe charring on the sides facing the fire. Reconstruction began in January 2024, and residents began moving in last summer. The post Former Burned Out Charlotte Apartments Trade for Nearly $500K/Unit appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.title: Atlanta Church Buys 94K-SF Buckhead Office Building
stories.excerpt: Transwestern brokered the acquisition of Piedmont Place, a 94,000-square-foot, four-story office building at 3520 Piedmont Road Northeast in Atlanta. Transwestern’s Bradley Fulkerson and Austin Hibbard represented Christ Covenant Church, which acquired the property from Hall Capital for $16.9 million, or $179 a square foot. Transwestern has also been retained to provide Agency Leasing and Asset Services for the Class A Buckhead property. “Since 2017, Christ Covenant Church has grown to more than 2,000 members and three campuses in metro Atlanta. At Piedmont Place, the Church has an opportunity to build a central gathering place to serve its membership today and reach the City of Atlanta well into the future,” said Jason Dees, Senior Pastor at Christ Covenant.  Built in 1983, Christ Covenant plans to operate the property as a multi-tenant office building in the short term and develop a long-term campus, including the addition of a 2,500-seat sanctuary. stories.title: Cellular Provider InfiniG Secures $5M Seed Funding
stories.excerpt: InfiniG, an enterprise cellular platform for commercial real estate, announced Tuesday that it has raised a $5.2 million seed round. Early-stage venture capital firms J2 Ventures and Stormbreaker Ventures led the round. Los Gatos, Calif.-based InfiniG said it will use the funding to expand its mobile coverage as a service (MCaaS) product rollouts, automate mobile-operator integration, scale its InfiniG Insights, and advance the platform’s automation and physical artificial intelligence. InfiniG’s MCaaS platform enables building owners to deploy neutral-host, multicarrier indoor cellular coverage without the complexity and cost of traditional distributed antenna systems, according to the company. The platform also creates an upgradeable foundation for future 5G services, private wireless networks, physical AI and connected-building applications. “The mobile operators — the AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobiles of the world — have traditionally provided coverage,” said Joel Lindholm, co-founder and CEO at InfiniG. “The processes that have been used for the last 10 to 20 years really require people to come into each building using those processes and their own technologies, and that’s been very limiting. That’s why only the biggest buildings or biggest venues have coverage. That’s also why you see most buildings in the United States do not have coverage, whether they be hospitals or hotels, offices, warehouses or manufacturing floors.” Lindholm’s firm stepped into the gap. “Our solution is focused on being able to cover those thousands of buildings instead of the hundreds of buildings from the legacy model. Fundamentally, we have to look at the world in a new way for the next decade. The 10- to 20-year-old technologies are just no longer satisfactory.” InfiniG uses Citizens Broadband Radio Service (CBRS), a non-carrier spectrum, to provide a single radio infrastructure in a building that is shared equally across all the mobile operators. stories.title: Samantha Atlas of Ash Staging: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: Staging can play a critical role in residential real estate. It helps to bring a model unit to life, and it provides potential renters and buyers with a glimpse of what their future home could look like. Successfully staging requires more than a properly positioned couch and some art on the walls. Enter Ash Staging, a luxury staging and model residence design business that has completed thousands of projects — including commercial and hospitality spaces — over the last 15 years, representing over $50 billion in real estate. Samantha Atlas, senior director of projects at Ash Staging, has been with the firm for nine years. She splits her time between Los Angeles and New York City, and helped to launch the company’s West Coast office. Commercial Observer caught up with Atlas in mid-August to discuss her time with Ash Staging and the value of her work in real estate. This interview has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: What is the mission of Ash Staging? Samantha Atlas: I’ve been with Ash for a little over nine years now, and really seen it grow. I run the L.A. office, and I joined the company at a time of growth. Since I joined, the story has been, “How do we continue to grow and change the narrative of what staging can be?” Generally speaking, for a long time the idea around staging has been neutrality — nothing with a serious point of view. I came to work at Ash because we sort of eschewed that. We want to imbue personality. We want our clients and our potential buyers of these homes to have an emotional response — it’s what drives us. We believe in the power of paint and will really push our clients to invest outside of the staging into the property to get it sold. stories.title: Proptech Seed Rounds This Year Are in Full Bloom
stories.excerpt: To the surprise of some, or perhaps many, proptech has reportedly drawn the largest number of $5 million to $10 million seed rounds across industries in 2026. To the surprise of no one, artificial intelligence has a lot to do with those seed rounds. According to a Crunchbase report published July 31, at the top of the scale with $10 million seed rounds are proptech companies such as Breezy, a Los Angeles-based startup offering an AI operating system for residential real estate professionals; Grotto AI, a Manhattan-based IT and Internet firm offering AI-based tools for leasing and renewals; and Hint, a Charlotte, N.C.-based AI‑powered home‑management platform for homeowners. There have been at least 15 proptech seed rounds in the $5 million to $10 million scale so far in 2026, according to Crunchbase, which did not provide an overall number of deals in the category. A Center for Real Estate Technology and Innovation (CRETI) report found 30 deals in the $5 million to $10 million range in the first half of 2026 totaling $207.3 million and representing 4.6 percent of funding across all rounds. Overall proptech venture funding reached $4.53 billion across 231 disclosed funding rounds in the first half of 2026, with a median funding round of $6.75 million. Compared with the prior year, the market was broadly stable. First-half 2026 funding was down 0.6 percent from the first half of 2025 and up 2.6 percent from the first half of 2024, CRETI reported. The total number of seed fundings industry-by-industry is an elusive number. However, according to Seedtable, a global intelligence platform for startups, a typical seed round across industries is $2 million (median), stepping up to $9 million at Series A and $20 million at Series B. Seed is the most common stage by deal count, accounting for 29,708 tracked rounds in 2026. 100 CEO Caren Maio.
